findings.who: A filer who made a section 6013(g) election in an earlier year, such as 2021, and that election is still in effect when the filer files an MFJ return for 2025 with the same nonresident-alien spouse.
findings.why_no: The gated question asks whether they chose to be treated as U.S. residents 'for 2025' and the help says the choice is made with a signed statement. They remember making the choice in 2021 and signing no new 2025 statement, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: i8960 p. 7: 'If you’re making the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election ..., check the corresponding checkbox.' i8960 p. 3: 'If you made a section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election to file a joint return for regular income tax purposes ...'
findings.fix: Ask whether a section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election was ever made and remains in effect for 2025, including an election made in an earlier year; do not require a new 2025 statement.

findings.who: A filer whose spouse was a nonresident alien for part of 2025 and became a U.S. citizen during 2025, and who made a section 6013(h) election to file jointly for that dual-status year.
findings.why_no: The gate helper asks 'At any time in 2025, were you ... not a U.S. citizen?' The filer focuses on the spouse's current U.S. citizenship at year-end and answers no, overlooking the part of the year before naturalization.
findings.irs_text: i8960 p. 7: 'If you’re making the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election ..., check the corresponding checkbox.'
findings.fix: Rephrase the gate as 'Were both you and your spouse U.S. citizens for the entire year?' or add 'including any period before becoming a U.S. citizen.'

locators: p. 3, "If you made a section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election to file a joint return for regular income tax purposes, but don’t elect to apply the joint return election for NIIT purposes"
p. 7, Line 1, "If you’re making the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election (see Election To File Jointly With Nonresident Spouse—Section 6013(g) or 6013(h), earlier), check the corresponding checkbox"
